name: Outlook, Family Week
description: The next few days as a family timetable: one column per day, every appointment tinted, patterned and initialled with whoever it belongs to. Who owns what is configured once on the Outlook Core page, from Outlook categories, title prefixes like 'L: Klavier', a word in the title, or the calendar an event came from. Recurring commitments such as school and office hours move to a narrow gutter so appointment titles keep the width.

cell_options.name: calendars
cell_options.label: Calendars
cell_options.help: Leave empty for your default Outlook calendar.

cell_options.name: members
cell_options.label: Show these people
cell_options.help: Leave empty for everyone. Set up the family on the Outlook Core plugin page.

cell_options.name: days
cell_options.label: Days to show
cell_options.help: Always starts today. Fewer days means wider columns, which is the quickest way to get more of each title on screen.

cell_options.name: hour_start
cell_options.label: Day starts at
cell_options.help: The window is fixed so the grid keeps its shape between refreshes. Anything earlier is counted at the top edge of its day instead.

cell_options.name: hour_end
cell_options.label: Day ends at
cell_options.help: Anything later is counted at the bottom edge of its day.

cell_options.name: routine_gutter
cell_options.label: Routine in a side gutter
cell_options.help: Draws events a rule marked as routine — school, office hours — as thin labelled bars down the left of each day, leaving the rest of the column for appointments. Turn off to draw them as ordinary blocks.

cell_options.name: show_location
cell_options.label: Show locations
cell_options.help: Adds the location under the title where a block is tall enough. Off by default: the title is usually the better use of the space.
